citations.name: habeas:coverage
citations.commentary:
This edge-only validation regression deliberately supplies no node
 contents. Its records assert selection dependencies only. Domain
 requires this callback, but reaching it would introduce an unwanted
 content read and fail this guard.

rationale:
The `habeas:coverage` citation on `node_content` is a valid coverage exception. It sits on an explicit function with a body, which the built-in allows. The justification is in fenced citation commentary, as the built-in requires.

The explanation is substantive and agrees with the source:
- `node_content` in `impl[GraphWithChangingEdges/Domain]` only calls `panic!("edge inspection must not read node contents")`. It is a deliberate guard. If the test ever reached it, the test would fail, so zero execution is the intended outcome.
- The test `agent_edge_tools_record_selections_without_validating_targets` only exercises edge behavior, through the `outgoing_edges` tool and `edge_fingerprint`. Its assertions are on `Dependency::OutgoingEdges` records and on lookup counts. Nothing in it reads node content, which matches the commentary's claim that the records "assert selection dependencies only".
- The impl block supplies `node_content` only because `Domain` declares an associated `NodeContent` type and this callback. I did not open the `Domain` trait to confirm that the callback is required.
- The reason is not just difficulty. Executing the callback would introduce an unwanted content read and break the regression's purpose.

The citation is a `cite` of a built-in, and the item carries no `impl` or `test` reference to it, so it is not redundant.
